Hey. I would like to switch from Win8 to Mint. The few things that have prevented this from already happening are: What happens to all my files I want to access on Mint? Like my movies, documents, pictures etc. Also, I use photoshop for work and have a subscription for Adobe CC. How can I use it on Linux?

Thank you for your help and time.
Question about my windows files, when switching to Linux..

Get a usb and transfer all your files onto that. Install linux and transfer them. Gather them all into one folder, right click on the folder, properties. Look at the size and that will let you know the size of the usb you need. You can use photoshop in linux through wine or install a windows VM, install it and use it though that.

Movies and pictures are platform agnostic and won't be any trouble on Linux. The documents should be readable with LibreOffice though there may be some differences in formatting for .docx files.

You may want to look at other photo editing software than GIMP but I had success opening Photoshop .psd files directly with GIMP, with some differences but all the layers were imported. This was three years ago, so things may have changed in the meantime.

With Wine you may be able to just run Photoshop directly on Linux. WineHQ lists Photoshop CS2 as 'gold' status.

An easy way to circumvent this is to create a Storage partition on your hard drive, or buy a separate hard drive altogether, and store all your important, long-term items there. When you've moved all your files to this new partition/drive, you can safely install any OS you want and access that partition/drive at any time, regardless of what OS you have running.

You should not have major issues with opening your files. With Photoshop, you can try running it in Wine. But if you can't get it to work in Wine, there isn't much else you can do. While I'm a Linux user and I love open source software, I understand the reality that many people have to use applications that can't run on Linux. This seems to be a major reason why people don't switch to Linux. If Photoshop can't run in Wine, perhaps install Linux and then use a Windows 8 virtual machine inside it.
The cheap way is to Partition Hard Disk best thing to do is but a second HDD

If you're okay with investing in more hardware, you should buy a second hard drive, and use that for your new system. You can take the original drive and put it in an external USB enclosure, or even use it as a secondary hard drive.

There are ways to resize your drive's partitions, etc. but there the miniscule chance of data corruption. Also, if you leave the original drive intact, you can always boot it up again if you want to for any reason.

What others have said about your files is right, but Adobe won't work in WINE, don't waste your time trying to get it running in WINE. You can try Gimp and see if it works for your needs. If not, you'll either have to dualboot or run Windows in a VM.

Think OS specific. Most general files will be no issue. Movie, Pic, Music will be able to be accessed with no problem. MS Office is in the gray area a bit, but so big that there will be 99% support with an open program like open office or libre. I imagine most larger programs like Quickbooks and whatnot would have a solution as well. The only real problems you'll run into are with things made specifically for MS like Autocad (who may have a Linux version, but you'll have to look into it), Many games, specific sewing programs, etc.

I respectively disagree.

While the Beatles began their career playing simple rock n roll style tunes, its important to keep in mind that that was the standard practice at the time.

In fact, most pop music those days came in the form of a single song that was very popular, and many different artists would release their own versions of that same song.

In fact, the Beatles were really one of the first big popular bands to break that mold - part of the reason they were so successful was because of the insane songwriting duo that was Lennon and McCartney - they were writing several songs a week even at the beginning of their career with the Beatles.

Then their music became more and more esoteric as time went on, innovating with vastly different instrumentation than the standards at the time , introducing musical elements from India (sitar, tabla drum) and experimenting with new instruments such as the Mellotron in Strawberry Fields Forever.

While you're free to dislike the Beatles music, I think it's hard to deny that they contributed in a huge way to the development and diversity of popular music.
